_comment: Shared error-message parity table for the two filesystem-sandbox ports (#148, D-010).
Read by servers/filesystem-sandbox/test/error-message-parity.test.ts and
servers/filesystem-sandbox-py/tests/test_error_message_parity.py, so both
ports are exercised against literally the same expectations rather than two
hand-maintained copies. Fifth table, after max_bytes_parity.json,
sandbox_parity.json, and the config-trim pair.
This is the ONLY parity surface a client actually reads. The other four cover
internals -- how a config value is trimmed, how a path resolves, what byte
budget is accepted. This one is the string returned when a call is refused,
and before #148 all four arms diverged:
case              TypeScript                                  Python
outside_allowlist sandbox refusal (outside_allowlist): /etc/passwd
sandbox_escape (outside_allowlist): outside_allowlist: '/etc/passwd'
input_null_byte   sandbox refusal (input_null_byte): a<NUL>b
sandbox_escape (input_null_byte): input_null_byte: 'a\x00b'
generic error     content must be a string                    value_error: content must be a string
Python repeated the reason because SandboxEscape.__init__ already puts
`{reason}: {input!r}` into the message and _error_message then prepended
`({err.reason})`. That half was a defect on its own terms, not a parity
preference.
The input is JSON-quoted on both sides -- JSON.stringify / json.dumps with
ensure_ascii=False. Measured over nine awkward codepoints (U+2028, U+2029,
U+0085, U+00A0, NUL, U+001F, U+007F, a lone surrogate, U+FEFF) the two
functions agree on eight. The exception is a LONE SURROGATE, which Python
cannot encode to UTF-8 at all and so cannot round-trip an MCP stdio
transport; it is deliberately absent from `cases` rather than pinned to a
value one port cannot produce.
U+2028 / U+2029 are also absent even though both encoders agree (both emit
them raw). Embedding a raw line separator in a JSON fixture two languages
must read byte-identically is a needless hazard for a property already
verified directly; the NUL row covers the escape path.
WriteForbiddenError and FileTooLargeError were ALREADY byte-identical and
are pinned anyway -- a parity table that lists only what was broken cannot
notice one of them breaking later.

cases.name: sandbox escape, input carries a space
sandbox escape, input carries a NUL
sandbox escape, input carries a tab
sandbox escape, quote and backslash in input
sandbox escape, non-ASCII input is not escaped
write forbidden (already in parity; pinned so it stays)
file too large (already in parity; pinned so it stays)
generic error, content must be a string
generic error, not valid UTF-8
cases.message: file is not valid UTF-8 text: /r/x.bin
cases.expected: file is not valid UTF-8 text: /r/x.bin
